summary: This unit teaches you to run a linen room in a villa, guest house or hotel: know the types of linen and uniforms, work out par stock, receive soiled linen and issue clean linen item for item, store linen so it stays clean and dry, inspect and sort it, count it in a stock-take, deal with an outside laundry and keep the room secure, safe and hygienic.

blocks.p: The linen room is the property's linen bank. Every clean sheet, towel and uniform that guests and staff use passes through it, and every soiled one comes back to it. If the linen room is well run, rooms are ready on time, stock lasts and money is not lost. If it is not, rooms are short, linen disappears and costs rise. This unit is for HOSPITALITY VILLA/PROPERTIES SERVICES LEVEL 2 trainees.
The unit is about **counting, recording, storing and keeping clean**. A linen room attendant must be accurate with numbers, honest with records and careful with hygiene.

blocks.note: How you are assessed: theory papers (multiple-choice questions, short answers and essays) and group practical tasks in the Centre's linen room: a stock-take and shelf set-up, and a linen exchange, inspection and folding. The assessor checks your counting, records, hygiene and safety.

blocks.note: Wash your hands well with soap and water after handling soiled linen and after you take off your gloves, and **before** you touch clean linen.
blocks.label: Safety

ul: **Never carry clean and soiled linen together** on the same trolley or in the same bag. Germs from soiled linen could pass to the clean linen.
Do not shake soiled linen: it spreads germs, dust and lint into the air.
A room attendant's trolley carries clean linen on its shelves and soiled linen in a separate bag.

blocks.note: In Jamaica's heat and humidity, a closed linen room can get hot and damp. Keep air moving, drink water, and report leaks or mould at once.
blocks.label: Jamaica

sections.title: Types of linen, uniforms and terms

head: Group
Items
rows: Bed linen
Fitted and flat sheets, pillowcases, duvet covers, mattress protectors, pillow protectors, blankets, bed runners
Bath linen
Bath towels, hand towels, face cloths, bath mats; pool and beach towels, bathrobes
Table linen
Tablecloths, slip cloths, napkins, runners
Uniforms and others
Housekeeping, kitchen, front-of-house and maintenance uniforms, aprons, curtains

blocks.p: Sheets come in sizes to fit the beds: **twin (single), full (double), queen and king**. Sizes vary a little by supplier. Look at the **size label** or the coloured stitching on the hem, which many properties use to tell sizes apart. Never guess a size.

head: Term
Meaning
rows: Fitted sheet
Has elastic corners that fit round the mattress.
Flat sheet
A plain rectangle, tucked in or laid over.
Mattress protector
A padded or waterproof cover over the mattress, under the bottom sheet, to keep it clean.
Bed runner
A strip of decorative fabric laid across the foot of a made bed.
Slip cloth
A small cloth laid over a tablecloth to protect it and be changed more often.
Terry
Looped cotton fabric used for towels and bathrobes.
Poly-cotton
A blend of polyester and cotton threads: strong, quick to dry and creases less.
Thread count
The number of threads in a square inch of fabric, often used to describe the quality of a sheet.
Starch
A laundry product that makes napkins and tablecloths stiff and crisp.
Requisition
A form that a department fills in to ask the linen room for stock.

ul: Hotel sheets are often poly-cotton, because it dries fast and lasts through many washes; towels are usually cotton, because cotton soaks up water.
A higher thread count usually means a smoother, finer sheet, but it is not the only measure of quality.
A uniform is issued by size and recorded against the staff member's name and the date.
A staff member who hands in a soiled uniform receives a clean one in the **right size**. Staff do not take extras, and uniforms are not taken home to be washed.
A lost or damaged uniform is reported and recorded according to the property's rules.

blocks.p: **Par** is the amount of linen needed to make up every bed or room **once**. A property never keeps only one par, because linen is in use on the beds, in the laundry and on the shelf at the same time.

head: Where the linen is
Meaning
rows: In use
On the beds and in the rooms
In the laundry
Being washed, dried and ironed, or at an outside laundry
In store
Clean and ready on the linen room shelves
Spare
An extra margin for stock that is being repaired, lost or condemned

ul: Most properties keep **three par**, or more, depending on how fast the laundry is and whether laundry is done on site or sent out.
A property that sends laundry out, or that has a long laundry turnaround, needs more par.
Hotels with a high number of arrivals each day need more par than a small villa.

flow: List the items needed for one room or bed
Multiply by the number of rooms or beds to find one par
Multiply by the number of pars the property keeps to find the total stock
Compare the total with what you count
Report any shortage

head: Example: a villa with 8 bedrooms, each with one queen bed
Calculation
Answer
rows: Sheets: 2 per bed (one fitted, one flat). How many for one par?
16 sheets
Total stock at 3 par
48 sheets
Pillowcases: 4 per room. Total stock at 3 par
96 pillowcases
Bath towels: 2 per room. Total stock at 4 par
64 bath towels
The villa counts 40 sheets. How many are short of 3 par?
8 sheets

blocks.note: Work every sum twice. Write the sum down: a wrong count in the linen room means short rooms or money wasted on stock the property does not need.
blocks.label: Tip

ul: Par levels are set by management. Your job is to **count, compare and report** when stock falls below par.
When stock falls below par, tell your supervisor in good time, so replacement can be ordered before rooms run short.

sections.title: Receiving soiled linen and issuing clean linen

flow: Put on gloves
Take the soiled linen from the room attendant, and do not shake it
Count it by type
Check for items left in it, such as needles, jewellery or phones
Sort it by type; bag blood-stained or infected linen apart and label it
Record what you received
Place it in the soiled area or send it to the laundry
Take off gloves and wash your hands

ul: Check for **items left in the linen**: needles, watches, phones and coins can hurt people or be lost. Record guests' property, such as a watch, and **hand it in as lost property**. Do not keep it, give it to the attendant or send it to the laundry.
Linen with **blood or body fluids** is bagged apart and handled as the property's policy says, usually in a marked bag.
Linen from a room with **bed bugs** is sealed in a bag, labelled and reported at once.

blocks.p: Most properties use an **item for item exchange**: the room attendant hands in soiled linen and takes the same number of clean items. This keeps the count right and stops loss.

flow: Receive and count the soiled linen from the attendant
Check the attendant's issue sheet
Count out the same number of clean items
Check the items are clean, undamaged and the right size
Record the issue on the sheet and ask the attendant to sign
Load the clean linen onto her trolley, separate from any soiled items
File the issue sheet

head: Situation
What to do
rows: The attendant needs more than the issue sheet shows
Ask the linen room to issue it and **record the extra issue**. She does not take it from another trolley.
The attendant has fewer soiled items than she asks for clean
Check why; record any difference and tell the supervisor. Do not issue more than were handed in unless authorised.
A new room is being made up
Issue by the room list and record it.
A staff member's uniform is soiled
Issue a clean one in the right size and record it.
A department asks for stock
They fill in a **requisition**; check it is signed and record the issue.

blocks.note: Never give out linen without counting it and recording it. Linen leaves a property through unrecorded issues more than through any other way.
blocks.label: Remember

blocks.h: Records kept in the linen room

head: Record
What it shows
rows: Issue sheet
What was issued to whom, how many, date and signatures
Soiled linen received
What was handed in and what was sent to the laundry
Laundry delivery note
What went out and what came back, with the counts
Stock-take sheet
What was counted and where, against par
Discard (condemned) record
What was taken out of use, why, and when
Lost property record
What was found in linen, where, when and to whom it was given
Uniform record
What was issued to each staff member

blocks.h: Where and how to store clean linen

head: Rule
Reason
rows: Store on slatted or open shelves in a clean, dry, airy room
Air moves round the linen so that it stays fresh and does not grow mildew.
Keep it off the floor and away from the walls
Keeps it clean, dry and free from pests and damp.
Keep it away from chemicals, the laundry and food
Chemicals can spoil linen and fumes and spills cause damage.
Keep the room locked
Prevents theft; controls issue.
Fold items the same way and stack by type and size
Stacks neatly, counts easily and is quickly found.
Label shelves by item and size
Quick, correct issuing.
Do not store linen in plastic bags on a floor or in damp spaces
Moisture is trapped and mildew grows.
Keep the room cool; no direct sunlight
Sun fades and weakens fabric.

blocks.note: Linen put away while still damp grows **mildew**: black or grey spots and a musty smell. It must be completely dry before it goes on the shelf. Check the room regularly for damp, leaks and mould, and report them.
blocks.label: Jamaica

blocks.p: **FIFO (first in, first out)** means the oldest clean linen on the shelf is issued first. New laundered linen goes at the **bottom or back** of the pile, and issuing is from the top or front. This makes all of the linen wear evenly, so that it lasts longer.

ul: Many properties let freshly laundered linen **rest** on the shelf for a day or so before it is used again. This lets the fibres recover and the linen last longer. It also lets any dampness dry out.
Do not put new linen on top so that it is used first. That wears out a few items while others hardly get used.
Fold each type of item the same way every time, so that stacks are even.
Fold so that the hem or label shows, making the size easy to see.
Do not overfill shelves: stacks should be neat and a safe height.
Do not put heavy items above shoulder height.

blocks.p: Linen is inspected when it is folded, and again when it comes back from the laundry or before it is issued. This section is about what the linen room does with what it finds. Repairing and recycling linen is taught in more detail in its own unit.

head: What you find
What happens to it
rows: A stain that may wash out
Back to the laundry for stain treatment and re-wash.
A stain that stays after treatment
Set aside as a reject; condemned if it will not come out.
A small hole, loose hem or split seam
Taken out and sent for repair, as a reject, until it is mended.
Worn thin, many holes or beyond repair
Condemned: taken out of guest use and recorded.
Mildew or damp smell
Rewashed if the property allows; condemned if it will not come clean.
Wrong size or an item that belongs to another property
Returned to its proper place or reported.

ul: A sheet with a small hole is never folded with the hole on the inside, and is never put back on the shelf with the other sheets.
A stained pillowcase is never used 'with the stain at the back', or ironed hard to hide the stain.

**Condemned linen** is linen too worn or damaged to use or repair. It is recorded in the discard record, and then recycled if the property allows, for example into cleaning cloths. It is never put back in guest rooms or burned.
The discard record shows why stock fell, and when to buy more.

blocks.h: Sending linen to an outside laundry

flow: Count each item by type
Fill in the delivery note with the counts, the date and the service wanted
Sign it and ask the driver to sign
Bag and label the linen; keep any blood-stained linen apart
Keep a copy of the note
When the clean linen returns, count it against the delivery note
Inspect it for stains, damage and shrinkage
Report any difference or damage at once and record it
Shelve it for rest and rotation

ul: Four pillowcases missing from a delivery are **recorded and reported** to the supervisor and the laundry. Do not take items from guest rooms to fill the gap, do not say nothing and never change the list to match.
Check the returned linen for iron scorch, tears, stains and grey colour. Damaged items are rejected and reported so that the property can claim.
Some properties put infected linen in a **water-soluble bag**, which dissolves in the wash so that no one has to touch it again.

blocks.p: A **stock-take** is a full count of all linen. It is done at **regular, set times**, such as once a month, and sometimes more often in a busy season. It shows the real stock, finds losses and shows when to order more.

flow: Plan the date and time, and tell the departments
Stop issues, or record them, during the count
Count linen **everywhere**: the store, rooms, floors, trolleys, laundry and the outside laundry
Count by type and size and write each count down
Add the counts to find the total for each item
Compare the total with the records and with par
Investigate and record any difference
Report the result and the shortages to the supervisor

head: Example: counting sheets
Number
rows: In the linen room store
In guest rooms (on beds and spare)
On floors and trolleys
In the laundry
**Total counted**
Records say the property should hold
**Difference**
8 sheets missing: investigate and report

blocks.note: Linen must be counted everywhere, not only on the linen room shelves. Linen in the rooms, on the floors, in the laundry and at the outside laundry is still the property's stock.
blocks.label: Remember

ul: Keep the linen room **locked** when nobody is working in it, to prevent theft and keep track of stock.
Only the staff the supervisor names hold the key. Do not lend it to a guest, a friend or a staff member who has not been named.
Issue only against a record. Never let a person take linen from the shelves unrecorded.
Report and record losses. Investigate large or repeated losses with your supervisor.
Make sure linen is not used as rags or for other jobs. A cloth made for cleaning is marked and kept apart.
Never take linen or uniforms home.

blocks.h: Common causes of damage to linen

head: Cause
How to prevent it
rows: Using linen as cleaning rags
Give staff proper cloths
Too much bleach or the wrong chemicals in the wash
Measure and follow the labels
Dragging bags along rough floors
Use trolleys
Storing it damp
Dry it fully before shelving
Overloading machines and over-drying
Follow the maker's limits
Sharp objects left in linen
Check before washing

ul: Report shortages of linen, a faulty trolley, a leak or mildew in the store to your supervisor straight away.
Keep chemicals and any open bottles out of the linen room, stored apart, closed and labelled.

I can name bed, bath and table linen and uniforms, and the terms for them.
I can work out one par and the total stock for a property.
I can explain why a property keeps more than one par.
I can receive soiled linen: wear gloves, count, sort, check for items and bag blood-stained linen apart.
I can explain why soiled linen is never shaken and why clean and soiled are kept apart.
I can issue linen item for item and record it, including an extra issue.
I can hand in lost property found in linen.
I can store linen on slatted shelves in a clean, dry, locked room, away from chemicals.
I can rotate stock using FIFO and explain why linen rests.
I can inspect linen and decide: re-wash, repair or condemn.
I can do and check a delivery to and from an outside laundry.
I can carry out a stock-take everywhere linen is held and record the difference.
I can keep the room secure and control keys.
I can work safely: lifting, fire, sharps, bed bugs and chemicals.

blocks.note: In essay answers, give the reason for each step. For example: 'I keep linen off the floor so that it stays clean and dry and pests cannot reach it.'
blocks.label: Tip

c1.title: Setting the par at a Negril villa
c1.text: A villa in Negril has 8 bedrooms. Each has one queen bed that needs 2 sheets (one fitted, one flat) and 4 pillowcases, and each room has 2 bath towels. The owner keeps 3 par of bed linen and 4 par of bath towels. The linen room attendant, Sherene, counts 40 sheets in all the places they are held.

c2.title: The exchange in a Montego Bay hotel
c2.text: Mid-morning at a Montego Bay hotel, room attendant Tricia hands in 18 soiled bath towels at the linen room. She asks for 20 clean ones, saying that one of her rooms needs extras for a family. Another attendant, Gary, comes with no soiled sheets but wants 10 clean ones for a room he says is short. The linen room attendant, Olivia, has the issue sheet in front of her.

c3.title: The delivery from the outside laundry in Ocho Rios
c3.text: An Ocho Rios resort sends 120 sheets to an outside laundry. When the clean sheets are delivered, the note says 120 but Everton counts only 114. Two of the sheets have brown iron scorch marks and four are grey.

c4.title: The damp store room in Port Antonio
c4.text: At a guest house in Port Antonio, the linen store room has a damp patch on one wall. Clean towels are stacked on the floor beside a drum of cleaning chemical, and the newest laundered sheets have been put on top of the shelves. A pile of sheets in the corner has black spots and a musty smell. The room is hot and stuffy, with no air moving.

c5.title: A stock-take in Mandeville
c5.text: At a Mandeville guest house, Ravia carries out the monthly stock-take of sheets. She counts 30 on the linen room shelves, 24 in the guest rooms, 8 on floors and trolleys and 10 in the laundry. The records say the guest house should hold 80. While counting soiled pillowcases she finds a gold watch in one.

c6.title: Keeping the linen room safe in Kingston
c6.text: In a Kingston hotel, a cook comes to the linen room with a soiled chef's jacket and asks for a clean one in size large. A new worker sits on the step of the linen room and lights a cigarette, with the door open. Later, a heavy bag of wet soiled towels has to be carried to the laundry. The key to the linen room is hanging on a hook by the door.

questions.q: Sherene is working out one par of pillowcases. How many are there?
questions.why: Each of the 8 rooms needs 4 pillowcases, so one par is 8 x 4 = 32 pillowcases.

questions.q: How many sheets should the villa hold at 3 par?
questions.why: One par is 16 sheets, and 16 x 3 = 48.

questions.q: Sherene counts 40 sheets. What should she do?
o: Do nothing, as 40 is close enough to 48
Report that 8 sheets are short of 3 par
Buy 8 sheets without telling anyone
Take 8 sheets from a neighbouring villa
questions.why: 48 minus 40 is 8 sheets short of par. She reports it so that the stock can be replaced before rooms run short; she does not order or borrow without authority.

questions.q: How many bath towels should the villa hold at 4 par?
questions.why: 8 rooms x 2 towels is 16 for one par, and 16 x 4 = 64.

questions.q: What should Olivia do about Tricia's request for 20 clean towels after handing in 18 soiled?
o: Issue 20, as she knows the family needs extras
Issue 18, and record 2 extra only if authorised
Issue 18, and tell her to take 2 from another trolley
Refuse to issue any towels until the shift ends
questions.why: The exchange is item for item. An extra issue must be recorded, and authorised if the property's rule requires it, so that stock can be tracked.

questions.q: How should Olivia deal with Gary's request for 10 sheets without any soiled ones?
o: Give him 10 and say nothing in the record
Give him 10 from the shelf, but only the oldest sheets
Tell him to take sheets from another room
Record it as an extra issue, with authority
questions.why: An issue with no soiled return is an extra issue and must be recorded and authorised. Unrecorded issues are the main way that linen is lost.

questions.q: What must Olivia do when she hands out the clean towels?
o: Count them out and record them on the issue sheet
Let Tricia count them herself while she looks away
Give her the pile without counting, to save time
Count them after Tricia has returned to the room
questions.why: Linen is counted out in front of the attendant and recorded, with her signature, so the stock record stays right.

questions.q: What should Everton do about the 6 sheets missing from the delivery?
o: Change the note to 114 so that it matches the count
Take 6 sheets from a guest room to make up the number
Record the gap and report it to the supervisor
Say nothing, as 6 is a small number
questions.why: Counts are checked against the delivery note. Differences are recorded and reported so that the laundry can find or replace the missing sheets; never change records or take sheets from rooms.

questions.q: What should happen to the 2 sheets with brown scorch marks?
o: Be put on the shelf with the others
Be rejected and reported for a claim
Be used in the cheapest room
Be folded with the scorch inside
questions.why: Scorch damage cannot be washed out. Reject the sheets, record them and report the damage so the property can claim from the laundry.

questions.q: What should Everton do about the 4 grey sheets?
o: Put them on the shelf, as grey is a normal colour for old sheets
Send them back to be re-washed and record it
Use them in the cheapest rooms first
Iron them hard to bring the colour back
questions.why: Grey sheets mean the wash was poor, not that the linen is finished. Return them to be washed again and record it, so that the laundry is told.

questions.q: What is the most likely cause of the black spots and musty smell on the sheets?
o: Mildew, from damp linen and a damp, airless room
Dust, from the cleaning chemicals nearby
Fading, from the sun shining through the window
Starch left in the sheets after laundering
questions.why: Damp, warm air without movement lets mildew grow. Linen must be dry before shelving, stored in a dry, airy room and the damp patch must be reported.

questions.q: What is wrong with stacking the towels on the floor beside the chemical drum?
o: It makes the towels too hard to count
It saves shelf space but takes longer to issue
The towels can get damp, dirty or damaged by the chemicals
It lets guests see the stock more easily
questions.why: Linen is kept off the floor, on slatted shelves, away from chemicals, so that it stays clean, dry and free from pests and damage.

questions.q: Where should the newest laundered sheets go?
o: On top of the pile, so that they are used first
On the floor in front of the shelf
At the bottom or back of the pile
In a room where they are never used
questions.why: FIFO means the oldest clean linen is issued first. New linen goes under or behind, so that all linen wears evenly.

questions.q: What is the total number of sheets Ravia has counted?
What should she do about the difference from the 80 the records show?
o: Investigate it, record the 8 missing and report it
Add 8 to her count so that the totals match
Ignore it until the next stock-take
Take 8 sheets from the guest rooms to cover it
questions.why: Stock-takes exist to find the real stock and losses. Record the difference, investigate where the sheets went and report it.

questions.q: What should Ravia do with the gold watch she found in a pillowcase?
o: Keep it in the linen room in case a guest asks
Record it and hand it in as lost property
Give it to a room attendant to look after
Send it to the laundry with the linen
questions.why: A guest's property is recorded and handed in as lost property, so it can be returned. It is never kept in the linen room, passed on informally or sent to the laundry.

questions.q: What should the linen room attendant do about the cook's soiled chef's jacket?
o: Give him three clean jackets so that he saves trips
Tell him to wash it at home and bring it back
Issue a clean jacket in his size and record it
Give him any clean jacket that is free
questions.why: A soiled uniform is exchanged for a clean one in the right size, and the issue is recorded against the staff member.

questions.q: Why is the new worker's cigarette a danger?
o: Smoke makes the linen hard to fold
Linen burns easily and fire spreads fast
It makes the linen room too warm
It changes the colour of the shelves
questions.why: Linen and lint burn easily. Smoking is banned in and near the linen room.

questions.q: How should the wet soiled towels be moved?
o: Dragged by the bag's string along the floor
Thrown down the stairs to the laundry
Lifted fast with a bent, twisting back
Moved on a trolley, or shared between two people
questions.why: Wet linen is heavy. Use a trolley or share the load and lift with bent knees to avoid back injury.

questions.q: A property sends its sheets to an outside laundry. Why does it usually need more par than one that washes on site?
o: Because sheets last longer when they are sent away
Because more is needed to cover the time it is away
Because the outside laundry keeps some of the sheets
Because guests prefer sheets washed off site
questions.why: Linen that is out of the property for days is not available to use, so more sets are needed to keep every room supplied.
